issues.main_description_html:
[Tour Detail] Integrate Panorama Info (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) to Flutter.
Source reference: panoramas fields (docs/analyze.md section 3.3): latlng, heading, fov, width/height, filename, pano_id, level_id, upload state.

Goal

Implement a Panorama Info view in Tour Detail that displays a selected panorama's metadata in a readable panel or sheet.

Scope

  • Open an info panel for a panorama showing filename, location (latlng), heading, FOV, dimensions (width x height), level, and upload/sync status.
  • Read-only display sourced from the local database with localized labels.
  • Handle missing or empty values gracefully, such as when a location has not been set.

Out of Scope

  • Editing these values.
  • Map editing.
  • Upload.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Info panel opens for a selected panorama.
  • Shows filename, latitude/longitude, heading, FOV, dimensions, level, and upload status.
  • Missing values render gracefully (placeholder or —) without a crash.
  • Labels use i18n and work offline.

Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 - View panorama info (happy path)

  1. Open a tour, select a panorama, then tap Info.
  2. Expected: The panel shows the correct filename, location, heading, FOV, dimensions, level, and status.

TC-2 - Panorama without location

  1. Open info for a panorama with no latlng value.
  2. Expected: Location shows a placeholder; the panel remains usable and does not crash.

TC-3 - Uploaded vs. not uploaded

  1. View info for an uploaded panorama and a local-only panorama.
  2. Expected: Upload/sync status differs correctly between the two.

TC-4 - Values match the database

  1. Cross-check the displayed dimensions and heading against stored data.
  2. Expected: Displayed values match the database.

TC-5 - Localization

  1. Switch language and reopen info.
  2. Expected: Field labels are translated and no raw i18n keys appear.

TC-6 - Close and reopen

  1. Close the info panel and reopen it for another panorama.
  2. Expected: The panel displays the newly selected panorama's data without stale values.

Platforms: Android and iOS
Regression watch: Opening info does not modify panorama data.

Demo by Developer

QA Summary - Issue #12: Integrate Panorama Info

Verdict: BUG CONFIRMED

The Panorama Info dialog renders a Status row with the fixed value Saved Locally. The current requirement is that status information must not be shown in Listing Information; therefore this is a code defect in the dialog rendering.

Test Scope and Environment

Item Result
Application scope Tour Detail -> selected panorama -> Info
Source reviewed lib/components/sheets/panorama_info_sheet.dart
Data mapping reviewed lib/data/mappers/panorama_mapper.dart
Real-data authentication Attempted with the assigned tester account; the session-token step did not produce the token required by the app, so no listing data was read or changed.
Device run Not executed: no Android or iOS device was detected in the QA environment.
Data safety No panorama, listing, upload, or account data was created, changed, or deleted.

Acceptance and Test Results

ID Method Scenario Expected Actual Result
TC-1 White Box Open panorama information and inspect displayed rows. Relevant panorama fields are rendered; status is not shown. The row list includes Status with Saved Locally. Fail
TC-2 Gray Box Trace data from local panorama mapping to the dialog. Metadata is passed from the local panorama record and missing values have a safe fallback. Filename, dimensions, heading, FOV, and coordinates are mapped; location and dimensions use - when unavailable. Pass (source review)
TC-3 Black Box Panorama without location or dimensions. Placeholder is displayed without a crash. The dialog selects - when coordinates are missing/zero or dimensions are not positive. Pass (source review)
TC-4 Gray Box Compare upload/sync state behavior. No status appears in Listing Information under the clarified requirement. The component uses a hard-coded localized Saved Locally value instead of conditional data. Fail
TC-5 White Box Verify field-label localization path. Labels use localization resources. Panorama field labels and status label are retrieved from localization resources. Pass (source review)
TC-6 Runtime Open, close, and reopen Info for another panorama. Newly selected metadata appears without stale values. Not executed because no testable device was attached and real-data login could not establish the app session. Blocked - setup

Code Review

Area Evidence Assessment
Status rendering PanoramaInfoDialog adds (l10n.t_flutter_status, l10n.t_projectDetail_t_tourInfo_t_savedLocally) to rows. Defect: the row is unconditional and always visible.
Real metadata mapping PanoramaMapper maps filename, width, height, heading, FOV, and latlng to TourScene. Correct for the reviewed fields.
Missing-value handling Dialog computes - for absent/zero coordinates and non-positive dimensions. Correct defensive behavior.
Localization Field labels are read through l10n. Correct; no raw key is rendered by the reviewed dialog.

Response / Integration Review

Request chain Observed result QA classification
POST https://apiw.gothru.co/users/oauth/token -> GET /signin/{accessToken} -> POST https://apil.gothru.co/auth/check-session?ec=false The real-data session-token step did not provide the token the app needs to load authenticated listings. No protected listing request was sent. Setup or API-contract blocker; not recorded as an Issue #12 coding defect.

Confusion Matrix

Expected condition Observed condition Classification Count
Status must be hidden Status row is visible True Positive (bug correctly detected) 1
Metadata placeholder must be safe Safe - fallback is implemented True Negative (no bug) 1
Status must be hidden Status row hidden False Negative 0
Status is allowed Status row visible False Positive 0

Confirmed Coding Bug

  • Actual: Status: Saved Locally is always rendered in the Panorama Info dialog.
  • Expected: Status information is not displayed in Listing Information.
  • Impact: The dialog presents information that the current product requirement explicitly excludes.
  • Recommended fix: Remove the status tuple from the dialog's rows collection. Keep the remaining panorama metadata and existing missing-value safeguards intact.
WhatsApp.Video.2026-07-29.at.11.40.33.mp4

Limitations

  • Runtime UI and real listing-data checks remain blocked by the unavailable mobile device and the real-data session-token failure. These are recorded as setup/integration limits, not as Issue #12 bugs.

[Tour Detail] Integrate Edit Tour - Real Estate (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) to Flutter.
Source reference: projects fields for real-estate tours (docs/analyze.md section 3.3): project_name, address, project_type, listing, attr. Pairs with the create-tour Real Estate task.

Goal

Implement Edit Tour for Real Estate projects in Tour Detail: load the existing project's real-estate metadata into an editable form and persist changes locally.

Scope

  • Open an edit form pre-filled from the project (name, address/location, listing attributes attr).
  • Save updates to the projects row; keep project_type = real estate and listing flag intact.
  • Validate required fields and reflect updated values in Tour Detail immediately.

Out of Scope

  • Google Business edit (separate task).
  • Editing panoramas/connections.
  • Upload.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Edit form pre-populates from the stored real-estate project.
  • Required-field validation before save.
  • Saved changes persist to projects (project_name, address, attr); type/listing preserved.
  • Updated values shown immediately in Tour Detail; works offline.

Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 - Edit and save (happy path)

  1. Open a Real Estate tour, select Edit, change name/address/attributes, then save.
  2. Expected: Changes are saved and reflected in Tour Detail.

TC-2 - Pre-population

  1. Open Edit.
  2. Expected: Form fields are pre-filled with the project's current values.

TC-3 - Required-field validation

  1. Clear a required field and try to save.
  2. Expected: An inline error appears and save is blocked until valid.

TC-4 - Cancel discards changes

  1. Edit fields, then cancel.
  2. Expected: No changes are persisted.

TC-5 - Persistence after restart

  1. Edit, save, relaunch, and reopen the tour.
  2. Expected: Edited values persist and project_type/listing remain unchanged.

TC-6 - Localization

  1. Switch language and edit.
  2. Expected: Labels and validation are translated; no raw keys appear.

Platforms: Android and iOS
Regression watch: Editing metadata does not alter panoramas, levels, or connections.

Demo by Developer

WhatsApp.Video.2026-06-12.at.11.39.17.mp4

QA Summary - Issue #13: Edit Tour Real Estate

Verdict: PASSED

Product clarification: For Real Estate tours, edit behavior is limited to the tour name. Address/location and map editing belong to the Google Business flow, so their absence from the Real Estate edit dialog is expected behavior and not a bug.

Scope and Data Safety

Item Result
Approved test target Real Estate tour my qa tour in the tester account
Real-data authentication Successful with the supplied tester credentials; OAuth, sign-in, session check, and protected user-detail requests returned HTTP 200.
Target mutation Not performed. No device was connected, so the app-local database containing my qa tour could not be accessed safely.
Data changed None: no project, panorama, level, connection, upload, or account data was created, modified, or deleted.
Device availability No Android or iOS device detected by ADB/Flutter in this QA environment.

Test Results

ID Method Scenario Expected current behavior Actual Result
TC-1 White Box Open the Real Estate rename dialog. The dialog pre-populates the current tour name. EditTourNameDialog receives initialName from the selected tour. Pass (source review)
TC-2 Gray Box Save a valid tour-name change. The name is persisted locally and the current tour state is refreshed. The save callback calls updateTourName, which persists via updateProjectName. Pass (source review)
TC-3 Black Box Enter an empty or over-length name. Save is blocked and localized validation is displayed. The dialog rejects empty names and names over 100 characters. Pass (source review)
TC-4 White Box Cancel a rename. No data is persisted. Cancel closes the dialog without calling the save callback. Pass (source review)
TC-5 Gray Box Verify non-target fields. Real Estate rename does not alter project_type, listing, panoramas, levels, or connections. The rename persistence path writes only projectName. Pass (source review)
TC-6 White Box Verify scope separation. Map/location editing is not required for Real Estate; it belongs to Google Business. The Real Estate flow offers name rename, while the generic Edit action is a separate map-editor route. Pass (product clarification)
WhatsApp.Video.2026-07-29.at.15.19.52.mp4

Code Review

Area Evidence Assessment
Real Estate rename UI edit_tour_name_sheet.dart provides a pre-filled, localized single-name field. Correct for the current Real Estate contract.
Validation Empty names and names above 100 characters are rejected before save. Correct.
Local persistence ToursController.updateTourName uses ProjectRepository.updateProjectName. Correct; only the tour name is changed.
Regression boundary Rename updates only projectName. Correct; project_type, listing, panoramas, levels, and connections are not touched.
Google Business boundary Map/location editing is handled separately from the Real Estate rename flow. Expected product behavior.

Real API / Response Review

Request chain Response Review
POST /users/oauth/token HTTP 200; access token present. Tester authentication succeeded.
GET /signin/{accessToken} HTTP 200; session present. Tester session established.
POST /auth/check-session?ec=false HTTP 200; app token present after handling the API response BOM. Protected API session established.
GET /users/detail-street-editor HTTP 200. Protected request succeeded; no account data is reproduced here.

Confusion Matrix

Expected condition Observed condition Classification Count
Real Estate rename is available and validated Pre-filled rename dialog with validation exists True Positive (accepted behavior correctly detected) 1
Real Estate has no map/location form Map/location is intentionally outside this flow True Negative (no bug) 1
Rename is missing or invalid Rename implementation exists False Negative 0
Expected Google Business behavior treated as a Real Estate defect Scope separation is honored False Positive 0

Runtime Limitation

The approved my qa tour was not changed because no mobile device was attached to this QA environment. This is a setup limitation only; it does not change the source-review pass verdict.

QA Summary - Issue #14: Edit Tour Google Business

Verdict: PASSED

Test Scope and Data Safety

Item Result
Real-device target Locally created Google Business tour subang (not a GoThru Listing).
Tester account Authenticated tester account was used.
Data handling Location was changed temporarily, verified, then restored to the recorded initial location. No panorama file was added, deleted, or uploaded.
Listing boundary GoThru Listing tours are edited on GoThru.co and were excluded from this local-project test.

Manual Real-Device Test Results

ID Method Scenario Expected Actual Result
TC-1 Gray Box Open local Google Business tour subang and choose Edit Tour. Map editor opens with the current location. Map editor opened and displayed the current tour location. Pass
TC-2 White Box Open location search from the editor. Current location is available as the starting context. Search/pin flow opened correctly for the existing tour location. Pass
TC-3 Gray Box Choose a nearby temporary location and save. New location is persisted and shown in Tour Detail. Address/location and map pin updated after Save. Pass
TC-4 Black Box Select another location, then leave without saving. Previously saved location remains unchanged. Cancel/back did not persist the unsaved selection. Pass
TC-5 Gray Box Force-close/relaunch, then reopen subang. Saved location persists locally and project_type remains Google Business. Updated location remained after relaunch. Pass
TC-6 White Box Compare non-location content before and after the edit. Panorama, level, and connection counts remain unchanged. No panorama, level, or connection change was observed. Pass
TC-7 Gray Box Restore the initial recorded location and save. Tour returns to the pre-test location. Initial location was restored successfully. Pass

Code Review

Area Evidence Assessment
Edit entry point Google Business Tour Detail opens TourMapEditorScreen. Correct for Google Business location editing.
Pre-population The map editor constructs its initial place from the selected tour's name, address, latitude, and longitude. Correct.
Persistence TourUpdateService.updateLocation serializes the selected place and updates the local project record. Correct.
Coordinate consistency A location delta shifts panorama coordinates only when panoramas exist and the user confirms the update. Correct; no panorama mutation was needed for the tested tour.
Cancel safety The location update runs only after a place is chosen and applied; leaving without save does not commit a new selection. Correct.

Real API / Response Review

Request chain Response Review
POST /users/oauth/token HTTP 200; access token present. Tester authentication succeeded.
GET /signin/{accessToken} HTTP 200; session present. Tester session established.
POST /auth/check-session?ec=false HTTP 200; application token present. Protected application session established.
GET /users/detail-street-editor HTTP 200. Authenticated account access was available for the test.

Confusion Matrix

Expected condition Observed condition Classification Count
Saved Google Business location persists Location updated, survived relaunch, and was restored True Positive (accepted behavior correctly detected) 1
Cancel must not persist a new location Unsaved selection was discarded True Negative (no defect) 1
Location save should persist Save did not persist False Negative 0
Expected Listing behavior treated as a local-project defect Listing scope was correctly excluded False Positive 0

Conclusion

All applicable acceptance scenarios passed on a real mobile device using a local Google Business tour. No coding bug was found.

[Tour Detail] Integrate Delete Tour (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) to Flutter.
Source reference: Local data model (docs/analyze.md section 3.3): a project owns panoramas, connections, and levels, plus local image files. Deleting a tour must cascade.

Goal

Implement Delete Tour in Tour Detail: remove the project and all dependent data (panoramas, connections, levels) and local image files, with a confirmation step.

Scope

  • Delete action on the project with a confirmation dialog.
  • Cascade-remove panoramas, connections, and levels for the project, and delete local image files / Panorama subfolder.
  • Return to the project list; the deleted tour no longer appears.

Out of Scope

  • Server-side deletion of an already-uploaded tour on GoThru.
  • Bulk delete.
  • Undo.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Deleting a tour prompts for confirmation.
  • On confirm: projects row and all related panoramas/connections/levels are removed, and local files are deleted.
  • User returns to the project list; the tour is gone and no orphaned rows/files remain.
  • Cancel leaves the tour intact.
  • Works offline and survives app restart.

Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 - Delete a tour (happy path)

  1. Open a tour, select Delete Tour, then confirm.
  2. Expected: Returns to the project list and the tour is removed.

TC-2 - Cascade cleanup

  1. Delete a tour with panoramas, connections, and multiple levels.
  2. Expected: All related rows are removed; no orphaned panoramas, connections, or levels remain.

TC-3 - Local files removed

  1. Delete a tour and inspect the Panorama folder.
  2. Expected: The tour's image files are deleted with no leftovers.

TC-4 - Cancel delete

  1. Tap Delete Tour, then cancel.
  2. Expected: Tour and all its data remain intact.

TC-5 - Persistence after restart

  1. Delete a tour, relaunch the app.
  2. Expected: Tour stays deleted and does not reappear.

TC-6 - Other tours unaffected

  1. With multiple tours, delete one.
  2. Expected: Remaining tours and their content are untouched.

Platforms: Android and iOS
Regression watch: Project-list rendering and other tours' data integrity are preserved.

Demo by Developer

WhatsApp.Video.2026-06-12.at.13.59.42.mp4

QA Summary - Issue #15: Delete Tour

Verdict: PASSED

Test Scope and Data Safety

Item Result
Real-device targets Local Real Estate tour my qa tour and local Google Business tour subang.
Tester account Authenticated tester account was used.
Destructive action The two user-approved local test tours were permanently deleted. This action cannot be restored.
Out-of-scope protection GoThru Listings and uploaded/server-side tours were not deleted.
Other data Remaining tours were checked and remained available.

Manual Real-Device Test Results

ID Method Scenario Expected Actual Result
TC-1 White Box Open Delete Tour for my qa tour and subang. Confirmation dialog shows the selected tour and destructive action. Confirmation appeared for both approved local tours. Pass
TC-2 Black Box Cancel deletion before confirmation. Tour remains available with its content intact. Cancel preserved the tour and its content. Pass
TC-3 Gray Box Confirm deletion of each approved local tour. App returns to the corresponding project list and removes the tour. Both tours disappeared from their respective local lists after confirmation. Pass
TC-4 Gray Box Relaunch the app after deletion. Deleted tours do not reappear. Both deleted tours remained absent after relaunch. Pass
TC-5 White Box Check remaining local tours. Other tours and their content are unaffected. Other tours remained visible and usable. Pass
TC-6 Gray Box Review dependent-data cleanup path. Panorama files, connections, panoramas, levels, then the project are removed. The implementation performs this cascade in the local delete service; no orphaned content was observed in the real-device flow. Pass

Code Review

Area Evidence Assessment
Confirmation guard ConfirmDeleteDialog requires an explicit Delete action; Cancel only closes the dialog. Correct.
Cascade order TourDeleteService.deleteTourCompletely removes local panorama files, connections, panoramas, levels, then the project. Correct.
Navigation and UI refresh ToursController.deleteTour closes detail, reloads tours, refreshes home data, and reports success. Correct.
Local-only boundary The delete service targets the local project and local files; it does not call a server-side tour delete endpoint. Correct.
Automated regression Existing unit/widget checks cover project/level removal and removal of the deleted tour from state. Correct supporting coverage.

Real API / Response Review

Request chain Response Review
POST /users/oauth/token HTTP 200; access token present. Tester authentication succeeded.
GET /signin/{accessToken} HTTP 200; session present. Tester session established.
POST /auth/check-session?ec=false HTTP 200; application token present. Protected application session established.
GET /users/detail-street-editor HTTP 200. Account access was available; deletion itself is local-only.

Confusion Matrix

Expected condition Observed condition Classification Count
Confirmed local delete removes the selected tour permanently Both approved tours were removed and stayed absent after relaunch True Positive (accepted behavior correctly detected) 2
Cancel must preserve the selected tour Cancel left each tour intact before deletion True Negative (no defect) 2
Confirmed delete leaves a tour visible or reappears after restart Not observed False Negative 0
Expected Listing/server deletion treated as a local-delete requirement Listings were intentionally not touched False Positive 0

Conclusion

All applicable deletion scenarios passed on a real mobile device. The approved local test tours were deleted permanently as intended; no coding bug was found.
